failure_categories.interpretation: Fine-tuning improved readability and acceptance, but semantic preservation weakened. This indicates a readability-faithfulness trade-off.
failure_categories.mitigation: Retain the independent semantic verifier, reject number or negation changes, and require entailment thresholds before accepting simplifications.

failure_categories.interpretation: Simplified queries lost exact financial terminology, which reduced candidate retrieval quality.
failure_categories.mitigation: Use original queries for retrieval, or preserve exact financial and legal terms during simplification.

failure_categories.interpretation: Combining original and simplified text recovered part of the lost retrieval performance but did not exceed the original query.
failure_categories.mitigation: Prefer the original query as the primary retrieval query and use simplification only for presentation.

failure_categories.interpretation: The L-12 reranker produced the best ranking quality but required higher latency than L-6.
failure_categories.mitigation: Use L-12 when ranking quality is more important and L-6 when response latency is the priority.

failure_categories.interpretation: Reranking improved recall and nDCG, but did not improve the top-ranked hit rate over FAISS.
failure_categories.mitigation: Evaluate domain-specific rerankers or add query-aware financial terminology features.

failure_categories.interpretation: The final balanced FLB evaluation could not be built because several risk classes lacked enough unique source clauses.
failure_categories.mitigation: Acquire additional source documents for the deficient classes rather than lowering quality thresholds or duplicating clauses.

summary.main_failure: Simplification can improve readability while reducing semantic fidelity and retrieval effectiveness.
summary.main_recommendation: Use the original text for retrieval, simplify only for user presentation, and retain verifier-based gating.

limitations: The simplifier comparison used 20 held-out clauses.
The retrieval-query ablation used 30 FinanceBench examples.
The full balanced FLB evaluation remains infeasible due to class shortages.
